name: The Plaza Hotel New York
insider_take: This legendary Fifth Avenue icon has been the ultimate symbol of New York luxury since 1907, where Eloise ran wild and countless movies captured its grandeur.
whats_special: The Plaza is the only hotel designated as a National Historic Landmark, featuring 282 opulent rooms and suites with hand-painted ceilings. Its prime corner location offers unparalleled views of Central Park, Fifth Avenue shopping, and the bustling energy of Grand Army Plaza. The hotel's Palm Court remains the city's most prestigious spot for afternoon tea.
pro_tip: Book a Central Park-facing room on floors 10-18 for the best views, and make Palm Court reservations well in advance – they're nearly impossible to secure last-minute.
dont_miss: The legendary Oak Bar for craft cocktails, shopping at Bergdorf Goodman and Tiffany & Co. directly across the street, and taking photos at the iconic horse-drawn carriage entrance that's appeared in over 100 films including "Home Alone 2" and "The Great Gatsby."
pros: Iconic Fifth Avenue location overlooking Central Park
Historic luxury landmark with timeless elegance
World-class dining including The Oak Room and Palm Court
cons: Busy Midtown location with high foot traffic
